records.name: Lower Moyamensing Civic Association
records.summary: A volunteer civic group for Lower Moyamensing in South Philadelphia, the blocks roughly from Broad to 7th Streets and Snyder to Oregon Avenues. Members run a spring and fall flea market, a holiday tree recycling drive, and an environmental committee that organizes cleanups and tree care.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help run the flea markets and the tree drive, join litter checks and block cleanups, and help care for trees and neighborhood gardens. Paying members also vote in board elections and on other questions the board puts to the membership.

schedule.text: The group runs a spring and a fall flea market and a holiday tree recycling drive.

cost.text: Membership is $15 a year per adult. Joining the email list and volunteering are free.

first_step.how: Join the free email list, or email lomophilly@gmail.com to ask when the next general meeting is. Membership ($15 a year, for adults 18 and up who live or own property in the area) gives you a vote in board matters.
first_step.basis: Volunteer work is open to residents, costs nothing, and has a clear way in through the email list and contact, but meeting times and whether non-members can attend are not posted.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a meeting runs or who usually comes. The easiest first step is a block cleanup, where the group can help with supplies, or a quick litter check on trash nights. Check the calendar or the email list for the next date before you come.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's calendar page or email list for the next date.
Ask whether general meetings are open to people who are not members.

records.notes: The Fall 2026 flea market was held Saturday October 3, 2026 (the site's newest dated item, used for last_sign_of_life). The posting date is not shown. Membership is for residents and property owners aged 18 and up, applied for online or on paper, with each adult in a household filing separately. Meeting days, times, and whether non-members can attend are not posted on the site, and the calendar page lists no meetings. The 2437 S. Broad St. address is the office address on the City list and the membership page; the site does not say meetings are held there. Older 2014 and 2015 pages were not used for dates.

records.name: Manton Street Park Community Garden
records.summary: Manton Street Park Community Garden is a registered community garden in the South part of the city, listed by the City of Philadelphia. Neighbors grow food and flowers together; contact the garden to ask about a plot or a workday.
records.what_you_do: Garden alongside neighbors and help with workdays.

cost.text: A 2015 profile listed a plot fee of $45 a year. Ask the garden for the current fee.

first_step.how: Email mantonstreetpark@gmail.com to ask about a plot or the next workday. No workday schedule is posted.
first_step.basis: The only listed contacts are an email address and a Facebook page, and no workday schedule or plot process is posted, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: No current visit details are posted. A 2015 profile described neighbors weeding and watering the beds on workdays, and the group also held a yearly block party at that time. Ask the garden what is happening now before you come.
first_visit_tips: Email the garden before you visit, because no workday schedule is posted.
Ask about plot openings and the current fee, since the fee above comes from 2015.

records.notes: This garden has no website of its own. Tier 1 listed the Facebook page as its website; it now sits under social, and the Facebook page was not read. The City registry (2026) shows the garden still exists. The only dated facts about the garden are from a November 2015 spotlight on myphillypark.org: 10 beds, a $45 plot fee, and a neighborhood Friends group that runs the site. Status is set to unknown instead of dormant because the registry shows it still exists and no newer activity was found either way. A WebSearch returned mostly older news and a city parks stewardship contact; those search summaries were not opened and are not recorded here. Waitlist and cleanup-month details from the search summaries are not used.

records.name: MusiCoLab
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that helps local writers and composers build new musicals, with showcases and readings that audiences can attend.
records.what_you_do: Audiences can join the mailing list and attend showcases and the UP NEXT Spotlight Series. Writers and composers can look at the site's Submissions page to send in their work. Feedback is also collected through a page on the site.

schedule.text: Showcases and readings come up from time to time and are announced to the mailing list. No dates are set on the site right now.

cost.text: The site does not say what showcases cost.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on musicolab.org to hear about the next showcase. Writers and composers can send their work through the Submissions page.
first_step.basis: Showcases are open to the public and the site gives a clear mailing list sign-up, though no dates are set right now.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a showcase runs, what it costs, or who usually attends. The group describes its showcases as readings and selections of new musicals. Ask about the venue and the price before you go.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the mailing list so you hear about the next date first.
The April showcase dates listed on the site were postponed, and no new dates are set.

records.notes: The UP NEXT page names April 26 and 27 showcase dates at Arden's Horan Studio Theater as postponed, with no year and no new dates, so they are not used as dates. The 2025 workshop was public, with presentations on August 20 and 21, 2025 at The Drake, which sets last_sign_of_life. The contact page has a web form only (no email or phone is shown). The Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube links are the group's own.

records.name: Nichole Canuso Dance Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia dance company that makes and performs new work, and offers movement workshops for community members, dancers and students.
records.what_you_do: Attend a performance such as Lunar Retreat, or join a community movement workshop when one is offered. The company also brings workshops and lecture demonstrations to schools and community groups on request, and holds talks after its performances.

schedule.text: No regular class schedule is posted. Community workshops come up from time to time, and the company manager can say when the next one is.

cost.text: Ticket and workshop prices are not shown on the site.

access.notes: The company offered a Lunar Retreat workshop for blind and low-vision participants in March 2026. The site has no general accessibility statement.

first_step.how: Email Kat Moran, the company manager, at kat@nicholecanusodance.org to ask about the next community workshop, or buy a ticket to the next performance.
first_step.basis: Community members and dancers can take part in the workshops, and the company names a contact to ask about the next one, but no workshop is listed as upcoming.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 2026 Lunar Retreat community workshops ran two hours in the early evening, mixing movement prompts with writing, games, and group talk about care, grief, and change. The movement workshops focus on technique, improvising, and developing a grounded dance presence. The site does not list prices, experience needed, or room details, so ask before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask the company manager for the street address and the price before you come.
Ask whether the workshop needs any dance experience, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The Lunar Retreat premiere dates conflict on the site (Sept 9 to 20 on one banner, Sept 9 to 22 on another, and Sept 6 to 22 on the calendar), so last_sign_of_life uses only the September 2026 month. The March and April 2026 workshop dates are past and are kept out of the schedule. The IRS street number '1413' is incomplete and no street address is published anywhere, so the location is the zip only. Kat Moran is named as company manager on the workshops page. Prices are not posted.

records.name: North of Washington Avenue Coalition
records.summary: North of Washington Avenue Coalition is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the South part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: The coalition works on affordable housing, zoning, parking, and utility and tax issues for the area, with a goal of development that does not push out current residents. Neighbors can sign its petition and read its conservation overlay report and proposed guidelines.

first_step.how: Sign the coalition's petition, which is linked from nowacphila.org, or email northofwashingtonavecoalition@gmail.com to ask how to get involved. No meeting schedule is posted.
first_step.basis: Residents can sign a petition or send an email, but the site posts no meeting times, membership steps, or volunteer options, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe meetings, so it is not clear what a visit would look like. Most of the public material is reports and guidelines about zoning and housing, and news is shared on its Facebook page. Ask the coalition for the next meeting or action before you go.
first_visit_tips: Email first, since no meeting time or place is posted.
Read the conservation overlay report on the site to see what the coalition is working on.

records.notes: Tier 1 status was active, based on the City RCO list alone. The coalition's own newest dated item is the August 13, 2024 report (date taken from the file name), so status is set to dormant under the 24 month rule. The about page's history runs from 1989 to 2016 and was not used for status. No meeting, membership, dues, or accessibility information is published. The news link goes to Facebook, which was not read. Worth an owner check before the site shows this group as active.

records.name: Packer Park Civic Association
records.summary: A nonprofit civic association for the Packer Park area of South Philadelphia, north of Pattison Avenue and west of Broad Street. It works to improve living conditions and civic pride in the area, and the City lists it as a Registered Community Organization that is consulted on nearby zoning and building proposals.
records.what_you_do: The group reviews nearby building and zoning proposals with the City and developers, and sends neighbors emails and call alerts about local issues.

locations.label: Meeting place (per City list)
locations.address: City Life Church gym, 3301 South 20th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19145

access.notes: The City's registry describes this meeting place as accessible, with lots of parking.

cost.text: Membership starts at $25, paid once or as a subscription that renews every 12 months.

first_step.how: Sign up for the association's emails and call alerts on its website, and ask the group where its next meeting is. Membership, if you want it, starts at $25.
first_step.basis: The email sign-up and membership are clear, but the site posts no meeting times and its newest news is from 2022, so it is unclear what a newcomer would find.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical meeting or event, and its events list shows no meetings after 2021. Signing up for emails and call alerts is the simplest first step. Ask the group what is happening now before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether meetings are still being held, since the site lists none after 2021.
Confirm the meeting place before you go, because the address comes from the City list.

records.notes: Tier 1 status was active, based on the City RCO list alone. The association's own newest dated news is May 27, 2022, so status is set to dormant. Its events list shows holiday invitations for 2022 and 2023 (year only, no month), which are not used as the sign of life. The contact page lists john.goldbloom@gmail.com, undated; the City list address BCPACKERPARK@GMAIL.COM is kept because it is the more recent source, and the owner should confirm which is current. The membership page does not say who may join. The meeting place and access note come from the City list, not the group's site. The tier 1 address had the access note mixed in and has been cleaned.

records.name: Passyunk Square Civic Association
records.summary: Passyunk Square Civic Association is a volunteer-run nonprofit for the Passyunk Square neighborhood, which runs from Broad Street to 6th Street and from Washington Avenue to Tasker Street. It works on local history and character, neighborhood events, and small business support, and it follows zoning and development plans in the area.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors can attend the monthly general membership meetings and the free zoning meetings, join the yearly tree plantings and tree-cycling, and fill in the get-involved form so a volunteer can follow up.

schedule.text: General membership meetings are held on the first Tuesday of most months (not July or August) at 6:30 pm. Tree plantings happen each April and November, tree-cycling each January, and board elections each May. A sidewalk sale runs twice a year. Zoning meetings are free and open to the public, but the site does not give their day or time.

locations.label: General membership meetings
locations.address: South Philadelphia Older Adult Center, 1430 E. Passyunk Avenue, Philadelphia, PA

locations.label: Zoning meetings (per City list)
locations.address: St. Maron Maronite Church, 1013 Ellsworth Street, Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: General and zoning meetings are free. The site asks for donations to support its programs.

first_step.how: Come to the general membership meeting on the first Tuesday of the month at 6:30 pm at the older adult center on Passyunk Avenue, or fill in the get-involved form on passyunk.org or email contact@passyunk.org.
first_step.basis: The group says any resident or business owner can take part, whether longtime or new to the area, and it gives a form and an email to start. General and zoning meetings are free and open to the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: General membership meetings are held in person at the South Philadelphia Older Adult Center, and speaker notices usually go out by email and Facebook the Friday before. Zoning meetings are free and open to the public. The site does not say how long meetings run.
first_visit_tips: Watch for the speaker notice by email or Facebook the Friday before the meeting.
Ask where the zoning meetings are held, since the site does not list a place.

records.notes: passyunksquare.org redirects (301) to www.passyunk.org, so the website is updated. Status changed from active to probably_active: the group's own site has no dated news or events, only recurring items. last_sign_of_life and sign_of_life_url are left as tier 1 had them (City list, 2026-10), so the owner may want to clear them. The group's site asks for questions to go to contact@passyunk.org; the City list email dbgoldfarb@gmail.com is kept here. The zoning meeting place comes from the City list only.

notes: Seven groups, all verdict publish. Searches used 1 of 1 (hard cap). WebFetch used 24 times, within the 6 per group limit.
